title: How the hell did they make your turn to die?

posts.author: realdarkreunion
posts.body: I am new to RPG Maker MZ and MV and I am exploring everything they got but am really confused on how they even made Your turn to die. That game made me inspired on making my own game on rpg maker and I am planning on making a point and click with minigames, numerous choices and different endings. I am struggling with letting the player interract with the screen and unlocking new events, making a walk button and settings button when the monolouges are done ane ect, and I am having a hard time finding tutorials that could easen my problems. Any recommendations or tips?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
almost all minigames are done by eventing, although sometimes with assistance from plugins or scripts.
and all events are logic structures, which means you need to get the basics of eventing before you can try for specific sequences.
it is almost impossible to find tutorials for tiny parts of events, as those usually become obvious as soon as you get the big package understanding.
I suggest you first work through the build-in tutorials of the editor, taking special not of the parts where events are explained.
then perhaps look for general eventing tutorials and work through them - several older ones are linked in my "starting point" tutorial in my signature. they were originally made for VXA, but eventing has been unchanged since then. MV and MZ have only minor comfort updates to event commands, nothing really changed there since VXA

posts.author: ValentinaSama67
posts.body:
I'm pretty sure Echo607 has a series where she shows
how she made a visual novel in RMMV
and which plugins she used. She's no longer active in the community but maybe that can help you! And like Andar said, once you better understand variables, switches, common events and how to better use and adapt plugins to your needs, how to make these things will be very clear.
